label: copy phase: input l (or w) when w is being / about to be output, late in recall
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token (the token just copied back) is l (87% of mass) or w (13%). It is strongest on the copy-phase step where l is input and w is the next token to output, i.e. reproducing an original l-w bigram. Top activations are sequences ending in ...l w w, with the l step near the end of recall. It also fires weaker when w comes two steps later (l x w) and on w->w repeats. Weak tail activations show up on l inputs with no nearby w. It is nearly silent at recall_idx 0-2, even for l->w, and does not fire in the original or delimiter phases or on any other input token. In_tok=l & out_tok=w & recall_idx>=3 alone gives precision 0.88 but mass recall 0.68. The broader predicate trades precision (~0.5) for mass recall ~0.87. Activations are rare even inside the predicate, so some extra condition is still missing.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=l (+6.96), in_tok=l (+4.39), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+4.26), next_out=w (+4.16), phase=2 & out_tok=w (+3.86), out_tok=w (+3.68). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.97), recall_idx=1 (-2.79), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.79), next_out=h (-1.87).
